subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the 'bridge hold' used for when preparing food?
options: Forming a bridge with the fingers over the food and cutting underneath to steady small items
Curling the fingertips safely under the knuckles while slicing
Holding the knife at 45 degrees to sharpen it
Balancing the chopping board on the edge of the worktop
questions.explain: The bridge hold secures small round foods such as tomatoes by shaping a bridge with the hand and cutting through the gap.

questions.q: A recipe instructs you to 'julienne' the vegetables. What shape does this produce?
options: Thin matchstick strips
Small even cubes
Finely shredded leaves
Thick wedges
questions.explain: A julienne cut produces long, thin, uniform matchstick-shaped strips.

questions.q: When using the 'claw grip', which part of the hand is protected?
options: The fingertips, which are curled under the knuckles
The thumb, which is tucked behind the palm
The wrist, which is kept straight
The palm, which rests flat on the food
questions.explain: In the claw grip the fingertips are tucked under so the flat of the blade rests against the knuckles, keeping the fingers safe.

questions.q: Which cooking technique involves briefly boiling food and then plunging it into iced water?
options: Blanching
Poaching
Simmering
Braising
questions.explain: Blanching part-cooks food in boiling water before rapid cooling in iced water to stop the cooking and set colour.

questions.q: What is the approximate correct temperature of the oil for deep-frying?
options: Around 180 degrees Celsius
Around 100 degrees Celsius
Around 140 degrees Celsius
Around 250 degrees Celsius
questions.explain: Deep-frying is normally carried out at about 180 degrees Celsius, hot enough to crisp the food without burning it.

questions.q: Which method of heat transfer occurs when a pan is heated on a hob and passes heat directly to the food touching it?
options: Conduction
Convection
Radiation
Evaporation
questions.explain: Conduction transfers heat through direct contact between the hot pan and the food.

questions.q: Which piece of equipment is used to pipe cream or icing decoratively onto a dish?
options: A piping bag and nozzle
A palette knife
A pastry brush
A balloon whisk
questions.explain: A piping bag fitted with a shaped nozzle is used to pipe cream, icing or mash for a decorative finish.

questions.q: Why is it important to cut vegetables into uniform sizes before cooking?
options: So that the pieces cook evenly in the same time
So that the pieces contain more vitamins
So that the knife stays sharper for longer
So that the food weighs less when served
questions.explain: Uniform pieces cook at the same rate, giving an evenly cooked result with a consistent texture.

questions.q: Why is a sharp knife generally considered safer than a blunt one?
options: It requires less force and is less likely to slip
It is lighter and easier to lift
It cannot cut through skin at all
It cleans itself while cutting
questions.explain: A sharp blade needs less pressure, giving more control and reducing the risk of it slipping off the food.

questions.q: Why does steaming vegetables help to conserve water-soluble vitamins such as vitamin C?
options: The food does not sit in water, so fewer vitamins dissolve away
The steam adds extra vitamin C to the food
The high pressure creates new vitamins
The vitamins are sealed in by browning
questions.explain: Because steamed food is not submerged, water-soluble vitamins leach out far less than in boiling.

questions.q: How is heat mainly transferred to food cooking in a conventional oven?
options: By convection, as hot air rises and circulates around the food
By conduction through the oven glass
By radiation from the extractor fan
By evaporation of moisture from the food
questions.explain: In an oven, heated air rises and circulates in convection currents that cook the food.

questions.q: When food is cooked under a grill, how does the heat mainly reach the food?
options: By radiation, travelling in waves directly from the element
By conduction through the grill pan handle
By convection currents in cold air
By evaporation from the grill element
questions.explain: Grilling transfers heat by radiation, with infrared waves passing from the hot element straight to the food surface.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a well-chosen garnish?
options: It is edible and relevant to the dish, enhancing its appearance
It is always inedible but colourful
It should completely cover the main food
It must be the largest item on the plate
questions.explain: An effective garnish is edible, complements the dish and improves how it looks without overwhelming it.

questions.q: Why is portion control an important finishing skill when serving food?
options: It gives consistent serving sizes and helps manage cost and nutrition
It makes food cook faster
It removes the need for garnishing
It increases the vitamin content of the dish
questions.explain: Controlling portions keeps servings even, helps manage cost and supports balanced nutritional intake.

questions.q: You want to cook broccoli while keeping as much vitamin C as possible. Which method is most suitable?
options: Steaming
Boiling in plenty of water
Deep-frying
Roasting for a long time
questions.explain: Steaming keeps the broccoli out of the water, minimising loss of water-soluble vitamin C.

questions.q: A stir-fry recipe asks for carrots cut into thin matchsticks as a garnish. Which knife cut should you use?
options: Julienne
Brunoise
Chiffonade
Wedges
questions.explain: The julienne cut produces the thin matchstick strips required for the garnish.

questions.q: To give an unbaked pastry a glossy golden finish, what should you do before baking?
options: Brush it with beaten egg (an egg wash)
Dust it heavily with plain flour
Sprinkle it with cold water
Cover it tightly with foil
questions.explain: Brushing pastry with beaten egg glazes it, producing a shiny golden-brown surface once baked.

questions.q: You need to cook an egg gently in liquid kept just below boiling point so it stays tender. Which method should you choose?
options: Poaching
Vigorous boiling
Stir-frying
Grilling
questions.explain: Poaching cooks delicate foods such as eggs in liquid held just below boiling, keeping them tender.
